title: U.S. House · Florida's 12th District
area: West-central Florida in the Tampa Bay area, including parts of Pinellas and Hillsborough counties.

context.text: The Republican primary was canceled and incumbent Gus Bilirakis advanced unopposed. Kimberly Overman won the Democratic primary against Darren McAuley.

candidates.name: Gus Bilirakis

summary.text: Gus Bilirakis is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election to Florida's 12th Congressional District. A lawyer who owned an estate-planning practice, he served in the Florida House of Representatives from 1999 to 2007 before his election to Congress in 2006. He chairs the Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade and is running on his record of delivering federal funding and on lowering costs, according to his campaign website.

background.text: Graduated from Tarpon Springs High School and attended St. Petersburg Junior College, according to Ballotpedia.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Florida (1986) and a law degree from Stetson Law School (1989).
Owned a law practice focused on estate planning and served on the board of Lighthouse for the Blind, as a member of the Rotary Club, and in his local chamber of commerce before entering Congress.
Served in the Florida House of Representatives, District 48, from 1999 to 2007.

First elected to the U.S. House on November 7, 2006, and represented Florida's 9th District from 2007 to 2013 before the 12th District; in his Ballotpedia survey he names his father, former Rep. Mike Bilirakis, as his hero.
Serves as a senior member of the Energy and Commerce Committee and chairs its Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade Subcommittee; also sits on the Health and Communications and Technology subcommittees.

His congressional website says 78 provisions he authored have been signed into law and that the Center for Effective Lawmaking at Vanderbilt University ranked him the 31st most effective lawmaker in Congress.

priorities.text: Says he believes all Americans deserve access to high-quality, affordable healthcare and supports infusing free-market principles and cost transparency into the health care system rather than a government takeover.
Says the country is threatened by a debt crisis from unrestrained federal deficits and supports a Balanced Budget Amendment along with reduced federal regulation.
Supports an "all of the above" energy strategy that includes increasing domestic energy production alongside incentives for renewable energy development.

positions.summary: Supports an "all of the above" energy strategy that includes increasing domestic production, incentives for renewable resources, and conservation, and says the federal government should not pick winners and losers among energy sources.
positions.quote: Congressman Bilirakis firmly supports an "all of the above" energy strategy that includes increasing domestic production, providing incentives for the development of renewable resources, and promoting conservation.

positions.summary: Cosponsored H.R. 722, the Life at Conception Act (119th Congress).
Cosponsored H.R. 22, the SAVE Act, and H.R. 7296, the SAVE America Act (119th Congress).
Cosponsored H.R. 28, the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act of 2025 (119th Congress).

record.text: Assigned to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, chairing its Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade Subcommittee, and to the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, for the 2025-2026 Congress.

Cosponsored the Securing America's Future Act, providing a three-year renewable legal status for DACA recipients tied to ending chain migration, the visa lottery system, enhanced penalties for deported criminals who return, and border security initiatives.

candidates.researchNotes: Bilirakis has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; priorities and positions are drawn from his official House issues pages.

candidates.name: Kimberly Overman

summary.text: Kimberly Overman is the Democratic nominee for Florida's 12th Congressional District. A financial planner who ran her own advisory firm for more than 30 years, she served on the Hillsborough County Commission from 2018 to 2022. She says she is running on lowering costs, protecting healthcare, and government accountability.

background.text: Born in New York, New York; graduated from Woodrow Wilson High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Maryland in 1981 and additional education from the College of Financial Planning in 1988.

Spent more than 30 years as a financial advisor, earning the Certified Financial Planner designation and, according to her campaign website, building an advisory firm focused on ethical financial guidance.

Elected to the Hillsborough County Commission (District 7, at-large) in 2018, defeating Todd Marks and Kim O'Connor in the general election; served from 2018 to 2022 and lost re-election in 2022 to Joshua Wostal.

On the commission she says she chaired the board and served as vice chair of the Emergency Policy Group during the COVID-19 pandemic, and she also chaired the county's Affordable Housing Advisory Board and Commission on Human Trafficking.
Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary for Florida's 12th District with 52.7% of the vote, defeating Darren McAuley.
Describes herself as a mother, grandmother and small business owner, and says she became the legal guardian of her grandson in 2020 and later cared for her adult son until his death in 2023.

Has lived in the Tampa Bay area for more than 40 years, according to Ballotpedia, and lists decades of community service including the Seminole Heights Foundation board and the Hillsborough County Housing Finance Authority.

priorities.text: Lowering costs for families, including healthcare, prescription drug, housing, and insurance costs.
Protecting access to healthcare and strengthening Social Security and Medicare, and supporting caregivers.
Restoring trust in government through transparency and accountability.

positions.summary: Her campaign issues page says she will fight to restore and protect the right to abortion.
positions.quote: She will fight to restore and protect the right to abortion and access to reproductive care

statements.quote: She believes housing, transit, and child care are essential infrastructure—and should be treated as such.
Kimberly supports public safety policies that work: strong law enforcement paired with investments in mental health services, youth engagement, and community-led crime prevention.
She will work to lower prescription drug costs, expand coverage—especially mental health care—and protect access to reproductive services.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements come from The Issues page of her campaign website (third-person text). No debate or interview coverage was reviewed.

candidates.name: Branden Scrivener

summary.text: Branden Scrivener is running with no party affiliation for Florida's 12th Congressional District. He is 27, has a bachelor's degree in human services and has worked in healthcare for over three years, per his Ballotpedia survey.

background.text: Graduated from Sunlake High School and earned an associate degree from Hillsborough Community College and a bachelor's degree from Indian River State College; the two reference sources differ on the degree years, so they are omitted.
Has worked as a case manager assistant at AdventHealth since 2022 and previously as an assistant manager at Salt Life (2019-2022), according to BallotReady.
Is running with no party affiliation; BallotReady lists his stances on education, government reform, infrastructure and wages, including an 8-year term limit for the House.

priorities.text: Government reform: expanding Congress, term limits for members, and stricter guardrails on corporate campaign donations.
priorities.quote: focusing on policies which will expand congress, create term limits for Congressional members, and create stricter guardrails on corporate campaign donations.

priorities.text: Strengthening the Department of Education and fully funding programs such as Title 1.
priorities.quote: The Department of Education should be strengthened not destroyed.

priorities.text: Quality of life for the working class, including Medicaid and Medicare expansion, Social Security and lower housing costs.
priorities.quote: Quality of life for the working class should be our representative’s main driver in policy decisions.

positions.summary: Says voucher programs take funding from public schools.
positions.quote: Voucher programs take funding from public schools resulting in the closer of some schools, we’re seeing this within our own district.

positions.summary: Says he would advocate for expansions to Medicaid and Medicare.
positions.quote: I will advocate for a reformed healthcare system in the form of expansions to Medicaid and Medicare

candidates.researchNotes: Positions come from his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. No campaign website text or news coverage was reviewed.
